sections.h2: How did Murray County and its county seat come to be?
sections.html:
Murray County began in December 1832, when the Georgia General Assembly set aside the extreme northwestern corner of the state, land that had been part of Cherokee County, and named it for Thomas W. Murray, a former speaker of the Georgia House. Wikipedia notes that the original county was far larger and later shed territory to form Dade, Walker, Catoosa, Whitfield, Gordon and parts of other counties.

Spring Place served as the seat until the railroad skipped it. A Moravian mission opened there in 1801, and the Chief Vann House, built in 1805 for a Cherokee chief, still stands as a historic site. Cherokee removal in 1838 and 1839 opened the land to settlers. In 1906 the Louisville and Nashville line was built through the county's length, and Chatsworth grew up along it as timber and talc, discovered in the 1870s, moved out by rail. A countywide referendum in 1912 made Chatsworth the seat.

sections.h2: What natural landmarks mark Murray County?
sections.html:
Murray County covers 347 square miles in the mountains and valleys of northwest Georgia, and it is part of the Dalton metro area. Most of it drains to the Conasauga River, with the southeastern corner draining to the Coosawattee.

Fort Mountain State Park occupies 3,712 acres in the Cohutta Mountains, and the Chattahoochee National Forest covers much of the northeast, including the Cohutta Wilderness. Carters Lake, on the Coosawattee, spans 3,200 acres behind the largest earth-rock dam east of the Mississippi. Lake Conasauga, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1940 and sitting at 3,150 feet, is the highest lake in Georgia.

Chatsworth is the only city, and Eton is a town. Spring Place, Carters, Tennga, Cisco and Crandall are unincorporated communities. Fannin, Gilmer, Gordon and Whitfield counties border it, along with Polk and Bradley counties in Tennessee. Ask the commissioner's office which taxing districts cover your parcel, since an address inside Chatsworth or Eton may carry city tax.

sections.h2: What do Murray County's Census numbers show for housing and income?
sections.html:
An estimated 41,607 people lived in Murray County in July 2025, and owners valued their homes at a median of $180,700 across 2020 to 2024, per QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How do Murray County jobs and shops show up in Census data?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows 430 employer establishments in Murray County for 2023 and 62.7% of people 16 and older in the civilian labor force. Retail sales were $281,579,000 in 2022, health care and social assistance receipts were $66,857,000, and accommodation and food service sales were $37,928,000.

The average commute takes 28.4 minutes. Foreign-born residents are 7.0% of the population, and 13.4% of those 5 and older speak another language at home. Of residents 25 and older, 78.9% finished high school. About 1,732 veterans live in the county.

sections.h2: Where do Murray County residents pay and ask about property tax?
sections.html:
The Murray County Tax Commissioner is at 101 S 3rd Ave in Chatsworth, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 336, Chatsworth, GA 30705. Phone payments go through 470-289-4681, according to the county's online payment page, which a third-party company runs for card and e-check payments.

The county's FAQ lists (706) 517-1400, extension 1, for the tax commissioner and extension 2 for the assessors. The Clerk of Superior Court sits in the courthouse at 114 N. Third Ave, across the street from the commissioner's office, and holds warranty deeds. Murray County also offers digital statements and automated reminders through the online payment site.

The assessors' office is separate from collections. As the county puts it, the assessors do not take part in collecting property tax.

sections.h2: Which date does Murray County use, and what does lateness cost?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property tax are normally due December 1 in Murray County, which is earlier than the statewide default. Manufactured homes come due May 1, while vehicle renewals track the owner's birthday.

  • Interest runs at 1% a month once December 1 passes.
  • Balances still open 90 days later add a 10% penalty.
  • A homesteaded parcel owing under $500 is spared that 90 day penalty.
  • Past 90 days, the clerk's office can record a FiFa that credit bureaus may pick up.
  • The commissioner may levy on the property, which the office describes as a last resort.

Your printed bill controls. Murray's FAQ adds that a former owner who still receives a bill or notice may forward it to the new owner.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special programs does Murray County offer?
sections.html:
Murray County homestead exemptions are filed in the assessor's office rather than the commissioner's, at (706) 517-1400, extension 2. Documentation of ownership is required, and elderly exemptions require income verification.

  • Regular homestead: ownership and residence on January 1, with no income test, and filing online is allowed.
  • Elderly exemptions: several versions with different ages, filed in the office or by mail because of income checks.
  • Homestead freeze: available after one year of homestead, applied for in the office.
  • Veterans: the taxpayer must be 100% disabled during war, with Department of Veterans Affairs documentation.
  • Low income: household income below $15,000 a year, with documents.
  • Special assessments: Conservation Use, Preferential Assessment and Forest Land Protection, applied for January 1 through April 1.

Manufactured home owners who also own the land can claim homestead, get a free decal between January 1 and May 1, and pay the home's tax with the land tax. Other manufactured homes, such as rentals, buy a decal.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Murray County property value?
sections.html:
Mail or deliver a letter to the assessors inside 45 days of the Notice of Property Value Change. The county suggests certified mail or hand delivery, and the letter should explain as fully as possible why the value looks wrong.

The Board of Assessors studies it and replies in writing. The tax commissioner's FAQ describes the challenge as going to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator within 45 days of the notice, with superior court available afterward by written notice to the assessors. A state-certified five-member board updates county values every year at 40% of market value, and notices and bills follow the owner of record on January 1.

sections.h2: What happens to Murray County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Murray's assessor lists January 1 as the date of liability for ownership, so a seller who closes later in the year still answers for the full bill. No partial-year refund exists, the Department of Revenue says, so the contract decides how the bill is split.

Ask the tax commissioner at extension 1 for the balance on your parcel and any FiFa before closing. If the bill goes to a mortgage escrow account, ask your lender whether it has paid, because the assessor's office says collection questions belong to the tax commissioner. Need a warranty deed copy? The Clerk of Superior Court is across the street.

faqs.q: When are Murray County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Normally December 1, after which interest builds at 1% a month. Manufactured homes pay by May 1.

faqs.q: Which phone line serves Murray County property tax?
faqs.a: The county's FAQ gives (706) 517-1400, with extension 1 for the commissioner and extension 2 for the assessors.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for paying Murray County tax late?
faqs.a: Yes. Interest of 1% accrues monthly after December 1, and 90 days later a 10% penalty arrives, except on homesteaded parcels owing under $500.

faqs.q: Can I file a Murray County homestead exemption online?
faqs.a: Yes for the regular one. Elderly exemptions need income proof, so those go in person or by mail.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff to appeal a Murray County assessment?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the notice date, by letter to the assessors. The county suggests certified mail or hand delivery.
